server.instructions:
CandleStack is a lab for experiments on financial time series: a user uploads a trading model (Keras or ONNX), describes its input in a manifest and backtests it on market data, crypto from Binance and US stocks from Alpaca, then compares the results and publishes the good ones.

You act as the user who signed you in, with an API key or by allowing you on CandleStack (OAuth). The scopes of that sign-in decide which tools work: read (everything that only reads), backtests, models and publish. Call get_me first to see who you act for and what you may do. A tool that changes data says so in its annotations.

A tool answers JSON; its text leaves out the fields that are null. A failed tool call answers a problem as JSON: its type (https://candlestack.tech/problems/<slug>) names what went wrong and its detail says what to do; rate-limited also gives retry_after_s, the seconds to wait.

Answers about a backtest or a model carry its `url`, its page in the app; a comparison and a sweep of 2 to 4 backtests (a ranked sweep: its best 4) carry `url`, the app's Compare page with them side by side. Give the user these links whenever you show results, so they can see the charts and the details themselves.

Read the docs with get_docs (without a page it lists them) before you explain how the engine, a manifest, a metric or an error works, and answer from them: never invent a formula or a behaviour, and say so when CandleStack does not do something. A tool's full entry, with an example call: get_docs page mcp/tools, section <tool name>. Show metrics in a table. The server's prompts walk through common tasks. On the web: https://candlestack.tech/docs/agents/ and https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/; the resource candlestack://docs links them.

tools.description: Runs every check of set_manifest on a manifest for one of the user's models and keeps nothing. A dry run of set_manifest, which changes nothing. The checks: the form, the catalog (every block exists and sits in its step), the blocks' parameters, the names of the columns, the signature against the window and the columns, the shapes of the example, and the signature against the input and output read from the model file.

Each problem names its `field` (a path such as input.features[2].id), says what is wrong in `detail` and, when the check knows them, lists the values that fit there in `allowed`; at most 10, `more_problems` counts the rest.

The manifest's guide: https://candlestack.tech/docs/manifest/; its JSON Schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/candlestack-tech/candlestack/main/docs/manifest.schema.json.

tools.description:
Starts a backtest of one of the user's models (with a manifest) on one instrument and period: it runs at once or waits in the user's queue (one runs at a time, 20 wait). It answers at once: follow it with wait_for_backtest, then get_backtest.

The instrument: a stock for a model of US trading hours, a crypto pair for one of 24/7. decision is a threshold of 0 by default. get_backtest's `setup` has this shape, to run it again with changes.

Units: execution.stop_loss and position_size are fractions (0.07 is 7 %), fee_bps and slippage_bps basis points (10 is 0.1 %), not Settings' percent. get_backtest_defaults answers the user's defaults in these units too: pass them through for every setting the user does not name. Settings: get_docs page engine; results: get_docs page metrics.
tools.details:
One backtest of a user runs at a time and up to 20 more wait in the queue, and a few run at once over all users, taking turns; a queued one answers its place and `eta_s`. The run takes from seconds to minutes.

The arguments are the body of POST /api/v1/backtests: model.id (one of the user's models with a manifest), data.instrument.id (<market>:<symbol>) and data.period ([start, end) in UTC epoch seconds), and optionally decision (how the predictions become a signal), execution (fills, stop loss, position size, fees and slippage) and benchmarks (buy and hold of the instrument, or of SPY, QQQ or DIA for a stock). get_backtest_defaults gives the user's defaults as `period`, `decision`, `execution` and `benchmark_instrument`.

Pass an `idempotency_key` (a UUID you make) to call it again safely after a timeout: the same call with the same key within 24 hours answers the first backtest instead of starting another. Read the engine and metrics pages before you explain a setting or a result.

tools.description:
Compares backtests side by side, as the app's Compare page does: the 12 statistics with the best and the worst marked, and the setups with the fields that differ (a running or failed one has no values). `curve_points` adds the curves; with many similar backtests, `setup_mode="diff"` gives their shared setup once.

max_drawdown is 0 or below and a smaller fall is better: -0.05 is better than -0.20; the marks account for it. Statistics: get_docs page metrics; ranks: get_docs page sweeps.
tools.details:
1 to 20 backtests. Use it to pick the best of several runs; it reads only what each stored, so it is quick. Values that read the same count as equal. Each backtest has its `url`, and `url` is the app's Compare page with 2 to 4 of them: give it to the user to see the curves and the table.

`curve_points` (up to 200) gives the equity, drawdown and buy and hold of each on one time axis; without it the curves are null and `times` empty. setup_mode full gives each backtest's whole setup.

max_drawdown's best value is the highest one; its `better` says `lower` as in a lower fall, by its size. How sweeps and comparisons rank: get_docs page sweeps.
